published_ep_consensus_phase4.procedure: Rossi+2026 Sect.4.1 conservative approach: take all instruments, let the inter-instrument spread dominate the error.
published_ep_consensus_phase4.time_integrated: Fermi GBM CPL Ep = 283 +/- 7 keV (T0-0.064 -> T0+83.009 s, GCN 10944, PRELIMINARY) and Konus-Wind Band Ep = 264 (-40,+49) keV (T0 -> T0+102.144 s, 20 keV-2 MeV, 90% errors, GCN 10948) -> consensus Ep ~ 275 +/- 30 keV, error dominated by the spread. WARNING (T7): the two use DIFFERENT continua (CPL has no high-energy power law).
published_ep_consensus_phase4.peak_slice: Konus-Wind Band at maximum count rate (T0+1.280 -> T0+1.792 s): Ep = 383 (-82,+80) keV, alpha = +0.3 (-0.3,+0.5); Preece+2016 Ep,peak = 597 +/- 63 keV; Yu+2016 bin 5 (1.517-1.702 s) COMP Ep = 566.10 +/- 34.20 keV; Yu+2019 bin 1.19-2.25 s Band Ep = 376.80 keV. The peak-slice frame is 1.4-2.5x the fluence frame on this burst - budget for that BEFORE calling any Ep difference a discrepancy.
published_ep_consensus_phase4.suzaku_note: Suzaku-WAM fitted a SINGLE POWER LAW (index 2.15) over 100-1000 keV, T0-0.5 to T0+18.5 s - no Ep, and not comparable to alpha. Their 3% low-channel systematic and the XRS-Ne-dewar path caveat are stated in GCN 10950.

duration_component_coverage_T9.suzaku_wam: ~12 s, 100-1000 keV, emission T0-0.5 -> T0+18.5 s - MAIN PEAK ONLY
duration_component_coverage_T9.our_window: [-2, +32] s: covers the ENTIRE T50 span [3.712, 24.384] s and ~38% of the T90 span by duration. Every dedicated time-resolved paper stops at 20-30 s (Basak -1..22.6; Burgess -0.2..22.2; Li&Zhang -1..20; Yu+2019 0..30), so our coverage MATCHES the literature's; only Yu+2016 goes further and finds signal in just one bin past 21 s.
duration_component_coverage_T9.rule: Any T90 diff must name its frame. The GBM catalog 50-300 keV value (81.8 s) and Qin's 50-100 keV value (14.6 s) differ by 6x in nearly the same band - that is METHOD, not energy, and the Qin E^-0.20 scaling does not close it.

literature_bias_disclosure: Every dedicated analysis reads GRB 100707A as photosphere-dominated: Burgess+2014 (bright BB, 5 of 8 bursts), Iyyani+2016 (Gamma > 1000), Li+2019 (largest thermal-ratio variation in their sample), Li+2020 (hybrid jet), Acuner+2020 (P = 1.00, ln Z ratio 1013 - the most photospheric burst in their 36-burst sample). Basak&Rao 2014 independently measure mean alpha = +0.013 +/- 0.017, above the -2/3 line in 16/18 bins. This burst is STRONGLY PRIMED: a blind fit finding a significant BB is weak confirmation; a blind fit NOT finding one is the informative outcome. Disclosed so P3 can be read honestly.

30_minute_core: Acuner+2020 (2020ApJ...893..128A): Sect.3 + Table 1 row + Fig.2/3 captions ONLY. Our burst is the single most photospheric burst in their sample (ln Z ratio 1013, P=1.00) and their analysis interval is ONE bin, 0.36-0.70 s. This is the claim our blind fit is up against.

Burgess+2014 (2014ApJ...784...17B): Sect.4 + Tables 2 and 6. The sentence 'the flexibility of the Band function can mask the need for the blackbody component ... by having a harder alpha' is the exact mechanism our archival numbers reproduce (Band+BB LRT small where CPL+BB LRT is enormous).
next_30_minutes: Yu+2016 (2016A&A...588A.135Y): Sect.2 conventions FIRST (Ep vs Eb vs Ec; 'we should not compare the Band function's Ep or Ec to the SBPL's Eb'), then the 40-bin Table A.1 block for our burst - they report a per-bin BEST MODEL and SBPL wins 7 bins.
Li+2019 (2019ApJS...245....7L): Table A3 only (11 bins, kT and thermal ratio), plus the two flagged pathologies (kT~155 +/- 98 keV bins; dDIC = -7076.7).

Hakkila+2014 (2014ApJ...783...88H): the single paragraph on p.8 - GBM prefers a THREE-pulse solution for this burst, Suzaku a two-pulse one, and both admit one. Directly challenges our single-pulse sample criterion.
